ruling.recommended_action: Reject the rider's overcharge complaint and keep the metered fare as charged; no account flag on either party (driver's route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6 is not triggered). Advise Ryde ops that the geographic extent of the rider's "Sure, go ahead" consent should be clarified with the rider as a service-quality follow-up only, since the rider's refund claim itself does not succeed on this record.

segment_findings.reason: Post-consent deviation: driver asked at 14:29:20 to go round via West Coast Highway, rider replied 'Sure, go ahead' at 14:30:00; GPS shows the car on the routed AYE corridor until ~14:29–14:30 and on the West Coast loop only after 14:30. Rider's own timely message to the named route → RD-5 exemption; RD-4 not needed (traffic band 4 does not meet RD-4(b) band ≤ 2 and there are no incidents).

Remainder of the off-route travel through 14:43:10 (final re-join 1.2956/103.7762 → dropoff 1.2966/103.7764) is the continuation of the same consent route (RD-5); no separate unconsented detour is visible in the trace, and the residual vs the 8.569 km quoted route is map-matching/dispatch residual (RD-2: residual ≤ noise is not refunded).

rejected_claims.reason: 'The driver only mentioned the different route after he had already turned off' is contradicted by the timed chat: the driver's proposal is 14:29:20 and the off-route West Coast running is only from ~14:30:25 (GPS), i.e. the message precedes the turn-off (system records/time stamps override statements).

'I was overcharged for the extra distance' — the distance is metered (RydeTAXI) and the whole off-route portion was pre-approved by the rider under RD-5, so under RD-2 the metered distance figure stands; refund due $0.00.
